name: What office renovation scope is easiest to phase by budget?

mainEntity.name: If I cannot fund the full build-out at once, which office construction items can be phased later without redoing the work?
mainEntity.text: If I cannot fund the full build-out at once, which office construction items can be phased later without redoing the work?

acceptedAnswer.text: If budget is tight, phase the work that can be added later without tearing into completed construction. Finishes, furniture, decorative lighting, art, and some specialty millwork are often easier to delay. The items that should usually be planned early are layout, electrical rough-in, HVAC capacity, plumbing locations, and any code-related upgrades, because changing those later can mean demolition and rework. In Los Angeles office projects, phasing works best when the core infrastructure is sized for the final vision even if some finishes are deferred. For example, you might complete the reception area, main workstations, and one conference room now, then finish auxiliary rooms later. The contractor should coordinate phase boundaries so temporary walls, access, and inspections do not create extra expense. A good phasing plan protects cash flow without sacrificing the long-term layout.

The cheapest phase is the one that avoids tearing out finished work.
